solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dutch: 'Our solvers will have what it takes to do a Toughie'

definitions.text: what it takes to do a Toughie

indicators.note: the quoted words will have the letters inside them, running across the colon and quote mark, so they hold the answer

explanation.surface: The blogger Dutch reassures readers that they have the stamina to finish a hard puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch is the name of the Big Dave blogger who reviewed this puzzle, so the clue seems to quote him. The hidden run starts at the last letter of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough puzzle can take a long stretch of time to finish, measured in sixty-minute units.

clue.text: See 19
As is uniform in just about everyone?

definitions.text: As is uniform in just about everyone?

indicators.note: in places the uniform letter inside the shortened word for everyone
just about means almost, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: everyone means us all
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a matching style is found in nearly everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes what is customary: what is the same in nearly everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn or done the same way by nearly everybody is normal and customary.

clue.text: Cocktail Run is launched

indicators.note: launched means sent up, and in a down light that reads the pieces upwards

parts.note: to run a race is to race, past tense raced

explanation.surface: A cocktail is a run event being started.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy, orange liqueur and lemon mix is a classic mixed drink named after the motorcycle attachment.

clue.text: They 'enhanced' Crown Jewels, which chippy's cabinet displays?

definitions.meaning: Crown Jewels is slang for a man's genitals, and these Tudor pouches padded out the front of a man's hose
a chippy is a British fish-and-chip shop, whose heated cabinet shows portions of battered fish

explanation.surface: Something has been added to the royal regalia, and a fish shop is putting it on show.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is the padded flap of Renaissance menswear; the second splits the word into portions of a white fish.

clue.text: Sound of pigeon fillets in the oven or out of it?

indicators.note: to fillet is to remove the bones from the middle, so the central letter is cut out

parts.words: in the oven or out of it
parts.note: food in the oven, or on a hob outside it, is cooking

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether pigeon breasts should go in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fillets' looks like cuts of pigeon, but it is a verb taking out the middle, the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Doves and pigeons make a soft murmuring call, the verb's present participle used as a noun.

clue.text: News-gathering boarder? No pipes are calling him!

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so the pupil word gathers the letters for news

parts.note: a non-boarder at a British boarding school is a day boy
N is the abbreviation for new, so News is two of them

explanation.surface: A boarding pupil gathers news, yet nobody is calling him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes the Irish ballad: 'Oh Danny boy, the pipes, the pipes are calling'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Irish song opens by addressing a young man summoned by bagpipes, so he is its subject.

clue.text: Trading terms of Crown, truly a princess

indicators.note: the terms, the end letters, of Crown are traded, the first swapped out for the last

parts.note: truly means in fact

explanation.surface: Royal trade agreements are being described, honestly, for a princess.
explanation.walkthrough: Crown's ends are C and N; swapping C for N in IN FACT gives INFANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish or Portuguese king's daughter is given this title, the royal equivalent of a princess.

clue.text: One's at sea after hospital charges desert ship — he'll adapt

indicators.note: after puts the mixed letters behind the beast word
charges means rushes in, so the hospital letter charges into the beast

parts.note: the camel is the ship of the desert

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: After a hospital bill, someone abandons ship and goes to sea, adapting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert ship' looks like abandoning a vessel; it is the camel. 'at sea' makes EON from ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour-shifting lizard gives its name to a person who changes views to suit circumstances.

clue.text: First to swim across the pond finds recess

indicators.note: First to means the first letter of swim

parts.note: across the pond, from Britain, means in the United States, in US

explanation.surface: The first person to swim the Atlantic finds a resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity in the skull bones is an anatomical hollow, a recess.

clue.text: Conveniently lower figures about Newry and Mourne, say?

parts.note: about as a preposition means around, giving round
Newry and the Mourne Mountains lie in County Down, Northern Ireland, so the pair stand for that county

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up statistics for a part of Northern Ireland to make them look better.
explanation.walkthrough: Newry and Mourne was a council district of Northern Ireland, inside the old County Down.
explanation.definitionFit: To simplify a number to the lower nearby whole value is the arithmetic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Strain put on northen playwright

parts.note: to fray is to wear down or strain, as frayed nerves
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A dramatist from the north is under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Frayn is the English author of Noises Off and Copenhagen.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Frayn is a celebrated English dramatist, so the surname is an example of a stage writer.

clue.text: Flyer — League's Top Games — I am able to comprehend

indicators.note: to comprehend is to take in, so the games and the claim of ability enclose the league's first letter

parts.note: PE is physical education, school games
I am able is I can

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A leaflet advertises a sports league's best fixtures, and the writer says they understand them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' looks like a leaflet, but it is a bird; 'Top' picks the first letter of League's.
explanation.definitionFit: The large-billed water bird is a creature that flies, so it is an example of a flyer.

clue.text: New York City Subway's terminus attracts topless loony

indicators.note: the terminus of the word Subway's, setting the possessive aside, is its end letter
topless means the first letter is removed from the synonym

parts.note: loony means crazy, bonkers

explanation.surface: At the end of a subway line a half-dressed madman draws attention in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York City' reads as the definition of the big city, but Yonkers is a separate city in New York State; the possessive 's is ignored when taking the last letter of 'Subway's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonkers is a city in New York State just north of the Bronx, an example of a city there.

clue.text: 'Dial-a-Brief' cases given protection, Franco-style

indicators.note: cases means encases or holds, so the quoted name holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A legal hotline's clients are kept safe in the manner of the Spanish dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Franco' suggests the Spanish general, but Franco- means French here.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means under shelter, so sheltered or protected in the way the French would put it.

clue.text: See 19
The Sound of Silence — number on cassette and vinyl?

parts.note: a cassette is a tape
an EP is an extended-play vinyl record

explanation.surface: The Simon and Garfunkel song is tracked on old music formats.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title is the definition read literally: what silence sounds like.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for not even a tiny sound describes complete quiet, which is what silence sounds like.

clue.text: What timeshare affords? When merger occurs, bitterly regret actions

indicators.note: merging the two words lets the last letter of the first slide across the join into the second

parts.note: a timeshare provides a place to stay once a year, a pad yearly

explanation.surface: A timeshare scheme, and then a company merger leaves people sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: PAD YEARLY: the D crosses the word gap to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffer heavy consequences for one's deeds is to be badly punished for them, as with bitter regret.

clue.text: Made to feel the heat, took guard to secure Ashes?

indicators.note: to secure is to hold safe, so the batting word holds the vessel

parts.note: in cricket a batsman takes guard before facing the bowler, so took guard means faced
the Ashes, the England-Australia cricket trophy, is a small urn

explanation.surface: A cricketer took guard to protect the Ashes series under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the Test cricket series between England and Australia, its trophy an urn.
explanation.definitionFit: To be heated in a kiln-like oven is to be subjected to intense heat.

clue.text: Top double agent condemning silver as new school colour

indicators.note: new signals that the remaining letters are made into a new arrangement
Top here means remove the top, the first letter of the word double
condemning means rejecting, so the letters for silver are thrown out of the word agent

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A senior spy working both sides rejects silver in favour of a fresh shade for a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top double agent' looks like one spy; it is three pieces. OUBLE and ENT, mixed by 'new', give the light-blue shade of Eton College, the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College's pale greenish blue is the school's own shade, worn on its sports kit and ties.

clue.text: Taking in Afghanistan city ground a decent pace bowler's facing unenviable decision

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the mixed letters hold the city
ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: Kandahar is a city in southern Afghanistan

explanation.surface: A fast bowler with a city name faces a hard choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a cricket ground, but it is the anagram signal; the 's of bowler's is 'is'. This is the title of the memoir behind the film 127 Hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone caught between two equally bad options with no easy way out.

clue.text: Can Big Apple broadcast be good for this guy?

definitions.text: broadcast be good for this guy

parts.note: can and john are both slang for a toilet
the Big Apple is New York, NY

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a New York broadcast will improve some fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'be good' sounds like B. Goode, so the guy is the hero of Chuck Berry's song Johnny B. Goode.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock-and-roll hero of the Chuck Berry hit is called by this first name, followed by B. Goode.

clue.text: The tenth Médoc to be rapturously consumed

indicators.note: consumed means taken inside, so the wine words have the month inside them

explanation.surface: A tenth bottle of Bordeaux wine is drunk with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The tenth' looks like a count of bottles, but it is the tenth month of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: In the calendar it is the tenth month, coming after September.

clue.text: Could it be the Tour de France Express, suddenly showing little restraint? …

definitions.text: Could it be the Tour de France
definitions.meaning: split as ..., a mock-French phrase for the trip, the tour
to express oneself suddenly without holding back

explanation.surface: A rail express in France is let off the leash.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to speak or act without holding back, freely expressing anger or energy.

clue.text: Make Trump's No.1 suffer for his failure here? Suspend proceedings briefly

definitions.text: Make Trump's No.1 suffer for his failure here?
definitions.meaning: Trump's number one is his vice-president, the answer at 26; to suffer for failure is the answer at 16, so deducting a tenner from the number 26 gives 16
to pause for a short rest, as a break of a few minutes

explanation.surface: Someone wants a president's deputy punished for a failure, and the meeting is adjourned.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half works on the grid numbers: 26-across, the vice-president, minus ten becomes 16-down, bitterly regret actions.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop for a ten-minute break, a short pause in proceedings.

clue.text: … subject to snap?

parts.note: a snap is a snapshot, a pic

explanation.surface: Continuing the train, someone is liable to lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject to snap' reads as prone to anger, but 'subject' is a noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme under discussion is the matter of a conversation or essay.

clue.text: Names escape sexless author, minstrel's inspiration

indicators.note: the two name letters escape, leaving the word for sexless joined to the word for author

parts.note: sexless means neuter
a pen is a writer, here author
N is the abbreviation for name, so Names is two of them

explanation.surface: Pseudonyms slip away from a writer with no gender, while a singer finds a muse.
explanation.walkthrough: Names reads as plural words, but it is N's: two Ns, one dropping from each end.
explanation.definitionFit: Euterpe was the Greek Muse of music and lyric poetry, the goddess who inspires singers and players.

clue.text: The sauce has lost its duck, causing a row

indicators.note: has lost its means the letter is dropped from the sauce

parts.note: orange sauce is the classic match for duck, as canard à l'orange
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, O

explanation.surface: The sauce went without its duck, and a quarrel broke out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, but it is a line, as a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of mountains, or of things in order, is a series or chain.

clue.text: The VPD taking a break?

parts.note: split VPD into VP and D: the VP under Trump was Mike ..., and D is the old British abbreviation for pennies

explanation.surface: A police department is on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: VPD looks like a police force; broken apart it gives two readings: the US vice-president Mike Pence, and D, pre-decimal British pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Pence was the vice-president, and D was the symbol for old British pennies, the plural of penny.

clue.text: Who will mind nurses a little short of time with nitrogen safety device?

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the minder's word holds the next pieces

parts.note: a carer is someone who will mind another

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the time letter is taken off

parts.note: a bit is a little
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A question about who will care for someone, a nurse short of time with nitrogen supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like a noun, but it is the containment verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber's spring-gated metal clip is a piece of safety equipment for securing ropes.

clue.text: Doctor due in to lance man under restraint

indicators.note: to lance is to pierce, so the mixed letters pierce the word for man

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: to doctor is to alter or tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor is due to lance a patient who is being held down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the surgeon, but it is the anagram signal, giving INEDU from 'due in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held by chains is to be fettered, physically restrained.

clue.text: Were Carol and Oliver this tall and thin?

definitions.meaning: the film director Carol Reed and the actor Oliver Reed were both of the Reed family, so like a Reed
tall and thin, like a slender plant stalk

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether two famous relatives were lanky.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass-like waterside plants have tall slim stems, so the adjective describes someone lanky.
